newsitem.title: UK: Senior says this year "starts well".
newsitem.headline: Senior says this year "starts well".

text.p: Britain's Senior Engineering Group Plc said on Thursday that 1997 has started well following the sale of its loss-making thermal engineering division.
An exceptional charge related to the disposal of the division forced 1996 pretax profit down to 2.68 million stg from 22.13 million previously.
"Our new year has started well. With the thermal engineering division divested, the group is free to continue the successful development of its core businesses," said chairman Alan Watkins.
Underlying pretax profit at the company rose 38 percent in 1996 to 31.5 million stg with a total dividend payout for the year of 3.82p per share compared with 3.60p in the previous year.
Senior said its balance sheet remained strong with net debt down to 20.5 million stg from 22.8 million in 1995, representing gearing, its debt to equity ratio, of 16 percent.
The company had a busy start to the year on the acquisition front, with its Flextonics Unit buying U.S. aerospace technology company Ketema A&E from Ketema Inc for $23.5 million.
Senior made a total of 24.1 million stg in both acquisitions and capital expenditure in 1996.
